benchmark_type: deterministic real-container workflow; not an AI model benchmark

config.trial_order: interleaved correct/noop, reversed on odd trials

limitations: Known reference patches are deliberately supplied by a deterministic fixture; these are not model-generated solutions.
Three small teaching tasks check integration, not representative coding competence or a framework ranking.
No provider inference is made. Generic command token use and cost are unreported, not measured as zero.
Batch elapsed time includes image resolution, startup, transfer, agent execution, grading, and cleanup; no warmup is excluded.
Agent/grader times include Docker exec transport. Timing differences describe this host and image only.
With the default three trials, empirical nearest-rank p95 is the maximum; timing is not a confidence interval.
Grader files are withheld from the agent runtime workspace. Public pack tests are not secret from humans or model training.
Image tags may change. Actual immutable image IDs and source hashes are saved with every result.

cases.input:
Fix slugify(text) in solution.py. The function accepts a Python string and returns
a URL slug using this exact sequence: Unicode casefold, Unicode NFKD normalization,
then ASCII encoding with non-ASCII characters ignored. Replace each run of
characters outside ASCII a-z and 0-9 with one hyphen, and strip leading/trailing
hyphens. Examples: '  Hello, WORLD!  ' -> 'hello-world', 'Café déjà vu' ->
'cafe-deja-vu', and 'Straße 42' -> 'strasse-42'. Empty input and input with no
remaining ASCII letters/digits produce ''. Raise TypeError for non-string input.
Use only the Python standard library. Edit files in the working directory; a
written explanation without a working implementation is not sufficient.
cases.output: Fixture: applied known reference patch for slugify.

cases.input:
Fix stable_unique(values) in solution.py. Given a list of strings, return a new
list containing each distinct value once, preserving the order of its FIRST
occurrence. Equality is Python's case-sensitive string equality; do not trim,
casefold, sort, or otherwise normalize strings. Preserve Unicode and empty
strings. Never mutate the input list, and return a distinct new list even for an
empty input or an input that already has no duplicates. Example:
['red', 'blue', 'red', 'green', 'blue'] -> ['red', 'blue', 'green'].
Use only the Python standard library. Edit files in the working directory; a
written explanation without a working implementation is not sufficient.
cases.output: Fixture: applied known reference patch for stable_unique.

cases.input:
Fix merge_intervals(intervals) in solution.py. The input is a list of two-element
lists [start, end] whose endpoints are Python integers. Return the union of the
closed intervals as a list of two-element lists sorted by start. Merge overlaps
and intervals touching at the SAME endpoint, but do not merge an integer gap:
[[1, 2], [2, 5]] -> [[1, 5]], while [[1, 2], [3, 4]] stays separate. Handle
unsorted, repeated, nested, negative, and zero-length intervals. Raise ValueError
if any start exceeds its end. Return [] for empty input. Never mutate the input
or its nested lists. Every returned interval must be a new list, even when no
merging is needed. Use only the Python standard library. Edit files in the
working directory; a written explanation without a working implementation is
not sufficient.
cases.output: Fixture: applied known reference patch for merge_intervals.
